steps: Uncrate the stove
Remove the wood top, supports and plastic cover, unbolt the stove from the pallet (7/16" wrench), lay it on its back, then remove the 1" x 1/2" bolts (save them) and the pallet retaining brackets.

1. Carefully remove the wood top and supports.
  2. Remove the plastic cover.
  3. Using a 7/16" wrench, remove the lag bolts that secure the stove body to the bottom pallet.
  4. Place the stove body carefully on its back.
  5. Using two 3/4" wrenches, remove the 1" x 1/2" bolts and save them for later use.
  6. Remove the pallet retaining brackets from the stove bottom.

The rating label requires the appliance to be installed with the pedestal or leg kit attached (p. 3). Overall dimensions are given only as a drawing (Figure 2, p. 11).
Floor protection

Continuous non-combustible ember protection: USA 16" in front of and 8" to the sides of the loading door opening (min. 36" × 41"); Canada 18" on the firing side and 8" on the other sides (min. 43" × 51").
Position for clearances
Set the stove and floor protector to the clearance diagram (Figure 5). Never a makeshift or temporary install, never in a fireplace, never connected to an air distribution duct.

Select the position from the clearances diagram and set the stove and floor protection in place (Installation Procedure, step 1, p. 15).

  • Under no circumstances install the heater in a makeshift or "temporary" manner.
  • Do not connect it to any air distribution duct, and do not install it in any fireplace (p. 14).
  • Outside combustion air or fresh air into the room may be required in your area; consult local building codes.

Clearances may be reduced with heat shielding/insulating materials: consult CSA B365 or NFPA 211 and local fire codes and authorities. Local/national codes may override the manual. A WETT (Canada) or HEARTH (U.S.A.) certified installer is strongly recommended.
Chimney requirements

ULC-S629 / UL-103HT listed or lined masonry chimney with a 6" flue matching the outlet, serving no other appliance; minimum 15 feet system height; exit 3 feet above the roof and 2 feet above the highest projection within 10 feet.

Flue size6 inches (same as the stove outlet)
Minimum system height15 feet (4.6 m.), measured from base of appliance
Flue exit3 feet (1 m.) above roof; two feet (0.6 m.) above highest projection within 10 feet (3 m.)

Reducing or increasing the flue size may adversely affect performance. A masonry chimney must be lined, in good condition and meet fire and building codes; Figure 7 (p. 17) shows venting to a masonry chimney with a 6" S.S. liner and advises having it cleaned and inspected by a professional for cracks, weak mortar or other deterioration.
Locate & install the chimney

Plumb-bob from the exact center of the flue to mark the ceiling and roof, check joists and rafters, reconfirm clearances, then install the listed chimney from the ceiling to the rain cap per its maker.

1. Mark the hole position in the ceiling and roof with a string and plumb-bob hung over the exact center of the stove's flue pipe.
  2. Check that the location won't interfere with floor joists, ceiling joists or rafters. Adjust if necessary and reconfirm clearances from the stove to combustibles.
  3. Follow the listed chimney's directions to install the chimney system from the ceiling through to the rain cap; this may include framing in holes.

Figure 6 (p. 16) shows a residential system (spark arrester rain cap, storm collar, roof flashing, chimney support, wall thimble). An offset is allowed if all listed connector, offset elbow and chimney sections are screwed together with at least three sheet metal screws per joint and supported by the chimney manufacturer's listed offset support.
Connector pipe

Slip the crimped end inside the stove collar, crimps pointing down, and secure it through the collar holes; add lengths up to the chimney and join with the manufacturer's approved adapter (a slip section helps).

1. Slip the crimped edge of the smoke pipe (chimney connector) inside the stove collar and secure it through the holes provided in the collar.
  2. Install the remaining lengths one on top of the other up to the finished height of the chimney, securing them with the manufacturer's approved adapter. A slip section can make this easier.

Single-wall: six inch diameter, 24 gauge black pipe, clean and in new condition, as short and straight as possible, crimped (male) ends pointing down so liquid creosote or condensation runs back into the stove. Double-wall: install all components per the chimney/connector manufacturer. Figure 6 (p. 16) shows an alternate up-and-out installation and notes the unit may be harder to start; provide as much vertical length for the first section of pipe as possible.

Confirm the screw count at the collar: the manual says to secure every joint and collar with 3 sheet metal screws on p. 14, but to secure the pipe in the collar with two screws on p. 15.
Combustion air

Outside air through the 4" Intake Starter and 4" i.d. metal flex, from the floor or the wall behind: required for mobile homes (and alcoves, per the rating label), optional otherwise. Residential outside-air installs must be secured to the structure.
Wall pass-through (if used)
Use an NFPA 211 system: A 12" (brick), B 9" (insulated chimney length), C 6" (ventilated thimble) or D 2" (insulated pass-through) to combustibles; maintain the vapour barrier.

System A: brick wall, fireclay liner12 in. (305mm) to combustibles
System B: solid-insulated listed chimney length9 in. (229mm) to combustibles
System C: ventilated sheet steel thimble6 in. (152mm) to combustibles
System D: insulated chimney length as pass-through2 in. (51mm) to combustibles
  • A: minimum 3.5 in. (90 mm) brick wall with 12 in. (305 mm) of brick from clay liner to combustibles; fireclay liner minimum 5/8 in. (16 mm) wall, cemented in place, running to but not beyond the inner surface of the flue liner.
  • B: same inside diameter as the connector, 1 in. (25.4 mm) or more of insulation, 9 in. (229 mm) air space to combustibles; inner end flush with the masonry flue and sealed with non-water-soluble refractory cement.
  • C: minimum 24 gauge connector and ventilated thimble with two 1 in. (25.4 mm) air channels, separated from combustibles by 6 in. (152 mm) of glass fiber insulation.
  • D: chimney length 2 in. (51 mm) larger inside diameter than the connector, minimum 12 in. (305 mm) long, spaced 1 in. (25.4 mm) from the connector by sheet steel plates at both ends, 2 in. (51 mm) air space to combustibles.

Fasteners must not penetrate the chimney liner. Maintain the vapour barrier wherever the chimney or other components penetrate to the exterior (Figures 8-11, pp. 18-19).

Confirm connector pass-through: the rating label says do not pass a chimney connector through a combustible wall or ceiling (p. 3), while p. 14 allows passage through a combustible wall that conforms to CAN/CSA-B365 and pp. 18-19 give these NFPA 211 systems.
Mobile home extras
Double-wall connector and listed chimney only, outside air required, stove anchored to the floor (leg anchors and 1/4 -20 x 2" lag screws), never in a sleeping room.

• Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. Do not install in a sleeping room.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the mobile home floor, wall and ceiling/roof.
  • Anchor the stove permanently: hook the leg model anchors provided around the bolts in the bottom of the legs and secure them to the floor with 1/4 -20 x 2" lag screws.
  • Outside air supply must be used (Figure 6, p. 16).
  • Use a listed double-wall connector and a compatible ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney system, installed to the manufacturers' requirements. Horizontal connector not permitted in mobile homes (rating label, p. 3).

Clearances are in Figure 12 and on the Mobile home and alcove card.
Firebrick
Lay the brick pack: "E" bricks in the rear floor corners, "D" and "C" along the back, "D", "A" and "B" around the ash dump, then "D" bricks behind the rear and side brick rail tabs.

A1 1/2" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"
B4" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"
C7 1/4" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"
D9" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"
E9" X 4 1/2" w/ corner cut X 1 1/4"
  1. Place the 2 "E" bricks in the rear corners of the firebox floor (they fit around the two bolts), 2 "D" bricks beside them and the short "C" brick in the center against the baffle tube.
  2. With an ash dump: 4 "D" bricks along the front row, 3 on one side of the ash dump and 1 on the other, with the "A" and "B" bricks filling around the ash dump. Without an ash dump, use the extra "D" brick instead of "A" and "B".
  3. Slip 4 "D" bricks up behind the two protruding brick rail tabs along the rear wall.
  4. On one side wall, slip 2 "D" bricks up under the side brick rail tabs and push them to the rear, past the back brick; place two more "D" bricks in the remaining opening at the front.
  5. Repeat on the opposite side wall.

At each stage, close any gaps by shifting the bricks as the manual directs (toward the center, the baffle tube or the rear wall). Firebrick set part no. 80002223.

panels.title: Excessive creosote or dirty glass
items: Wood too wet → use dry wood
Air turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low → check for a plugged or restricted flue and improper chimney height and/or diameter; provide outside air; check and alter draft as needed
Dirty glass only: door gasket leakage → replace the gasket, check the door latch

panels.title: Low heat output
items: Wood may be wet → use drier wood
Fire too small → build a larger fire; open the draft control to raise the burn rate
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

panels.title: Won't burn overnight
items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred for overnight burns
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter; have a draft measurement taken

panels.title: Stove won't burn
items: Combustion air supply blocked → check the outside air supply for obstructions and that the room air cover is removed
Chimney plugged or restricted → inspect and clean

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
You light this stove by hand with newspaper and kindling. Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire.

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the stove and crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it. Add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open a crack, about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm), until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control for normal burning.

Your first 2-3 fires

The paint finish bakes on during the first few fires. The smoke and fumes can bother some people, so keep the room well ventilated: open all windows and doors. Follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) information sheet that came with your stove (p. 5).

Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures, or if the door is accidentally left open. Don't disconnect them.

burn.title: Air control, reloading and overnight burns
burn.html:
The air control sets how hard the fire burns. Every home's heating needs are different, so the right setting takes some trial and error. Note what works for future fires.

  • Smoke pouring down the glass (a "waterfall effect") means you turned the air down too soon or too low.
  • To reload, turn the air control to high and give the fire time to brighten. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff back into the room.
  • Mix wood of different shapes, diameters and lengths. Load it endwise, with room for air to flow between the logs. Always use dry wood.
  • Don't load wood so high, or in such a way, that opening the door becomes hazardous.

Overnight burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the wood completely on the maximum setting before you turn the air down for the night. To restart, rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to high. Once the wood has charred, reset the air.

Use the high "H" setting only to start a fire or preheat a fresh load.
Confirm the longest log: the manual says logs up to 18" (457mm) when loading (p. 7) but lists 20 inches as the maximum wood length (p. 3). Its ideal length is 16-18 inches.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
This stove is made to burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or green, freshly cut wood.

  • Season wood for six months or more and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out.
  • Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Never burn

Salt water wood, treated wood, wet, green or unseasoned wood, coal or charcoal, garbage, solvents, yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything containing rubber, plastic or asbestos, construction or demolition debris, petroleum products, paints, thinners or asphalt, and paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Salt water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the stove.

Test your wood

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. Dry wood burns on more than one side within one minute. Damp wood turns black and lights within three minutes. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's soaked: don't burn it.

safety.title: Staying safe around the stove
safety.html:
The stove is hot while it's running, and touching it can burn skin. Keep children, clothing and furniture away.

  • Hot glass burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away from the stove.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning. The stove isn't designed for open-door burning.
  • Burn directly on the firebricks, with no grates or andirons. Replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Never alter the air control. Tampering voids the warranty and can be very hazardous.
  • Don't store wood within the stove's clearances or where you load fuel and remove ash. Keep the area free of loose combustibles, furniture and newspapers.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended near the stove.
Don't over-fire. A glowing red top or vent pipe means the stove is over-firing. Pushing it past its design output can permanently damage the stove and chimney, is hazardous if not corrected, and may void the warranty (p. 7).

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the stove is cold. When ashes are 3" (76mm) to 4" (102mm) deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" (25 mm) of ash on the firebox floor to help keep a hot charcoal bed.

Ash chute

Pull the ash pan out about 2" (51mm), sweep ash from the ash lip into the chute on the right side, then close the ash pan.

Ash dump

  1. The handle is under the ash lip on the left. Pull it out 1/2" (13mm) and turn it clockwise to unlock the ash dump.
  2. Hold the handle open while you pull ashes into the opening. Avoid large embers; they still hold heat.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Make sure the ash dump door is properly engaged, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the floor.
  4. Lift and pull out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container, and replace the pan so it's seated properly.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Keep ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, on a non-combustible floor or the ground, well away from anything that can burn, until the cinders are thoroughly cool. Put no other waste in it.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
If the glass darkens from slow burning or poor wood, clean it with fireplace glass cleaner when the stove is cold.

  • Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape with anything that might scratch it.
  • Don't slam the door. Check that no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion and dry, well-seasoned wood, so your pipes and chimney are likely fairly clean. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That heavy deposit is building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the stove again. Use only 20-1/8" (511mm) x 11-7/8" (302mm) x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer. Don't substitute any other type.

chimney.title: Creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
A slow fire gives off tar and vapours that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites it burns extremely hot: that's a chimney fire. Some creosote is inevitable, so regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it's 3 mm or more.
  • Until you know your stove, check daily for creosote. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn dry, seasoned wood with plenty of air, and don't turn the air down too soon after loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens (p. 5)

  1. Get ready to evacuate. Have a plan everyone understands and a place outside to meet.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department. Have a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.

care.title: Maintenance checks
care.html:
Check these parts for cracks, excessive corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping:

WeeklyFirebrick (cracking); door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rail tabs and brick rails; air riser tube; back of the airwash chamber; baffle locking pin; boost tube cover
At chimney cleaningTop baffle board/blanket; baffle; top heat shield and mounting bolt; baffle gasket; brick rails; manifold
  • Door gasket: a 5/16" (8mm) fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure to seal. Replace it when needed with the kit from your Pacific Energy dealer.
  • Baffle (at the top of the firebox): some warping, up to 1/4", is normal. Replace it if it's warped more than that, cracked or broken. Never run the stove with the baffle or its insulation removed.
  • Keep the boost-air area at the front of the firebox clear of ash.
  • Clean a plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
Tell your dealer about any damage: running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty. Use only manufacturer-supplied materials for repairs (p. 9).

blower.title: Using the optional blower
blower.html:
If your stove has the optional blower, match its speed to the air control:

  • Air control on "L" (low): run the blower on "Low".
  • Air control between "L" and "H": use any speed you like.

Auto or manual

Auto: set the rocker switch on the side of the fan housing to "Auto" and choose a speed. The fan comes on as the stove heats up, and shuts off after the fire has gone out and the stove has cooled.

Manual: set the rocker switch to "Man" and choose a speed. This bypasses the sensor and gives you full control. You can switch modes or change speed at any time.

Keep it clean

At least every six months, vacuum the grill openings on the back and bottom of the blower casing to remove dust and debris (p. 10).

Keep the power cord away from the stove, and never run it underneath.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's limited lifetime warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensive, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (left out of the lifetime warranty). Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets aren't warranted.
  • Any part showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (such as high sodium content, plastics or chemicals) may void the warranty.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register your stove online at pacificenergy.net/register. The serial number is on the certification label or the manual's cover.

specEmis.title: Emissions, efficiency & heat output
specEmis.html:
EPA certified emissions1.8 g/hr
HHV tested efficiency74%
LHV efficiency80%
EPA BTU output13,567 to 39,159 btu/hr
FuelSeasoned cord wood

Certified to the EPA 2020 crib wood particulate emission standards using Method 28R. Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415; HHV includes the energy needed to vaporize the water in the fuel, LHV assumes it is already vapour. The heater has a manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate that must not be altered (p. 7).

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Outside airNecessary for mobile homes; optional for residential
Rating labelOutside air kit required for mobile home and alcove installations
Duct4"(100mm) i.d. metal flex pipe
Starter4" Intake Starter on the ash box enclosure

Through the floor: cut or drill a hole large enough for 4" metal flex behind the ash box enclosure. With the stove in place, attach the Intake Starter to the ash box enclosure and connect to the floor with the metal flex. The hole must draw from a ventilated crawl space or be ducted outdoors. Residential outside-air installs must secure the unit to the structure so the duct can't dislodge.

From behind: fit a 4"(100mm) air intake through the wall behind the unit, install the Intake Starter over the hole in the rear of the ash box enclosure, and run metal flex between the starter and the air intake.

Room air: the stove draws through the opening in the ash box enclosure. Keep the living space well ventilated; anything causing negative pressure can pull gases or fumes into the room. Figure 6 (p. 16) shows a 4" (102 mm) diameter air inlet with rodent screen; if the crawl space is well ventilated, it is not necessary to extend the air inlet to outside.

specBlower.html:
Kit#WODC.BLOWB

May be installed at any time; follow the instructions supplied with the kit. A rocker switch on the side of the fan housing selects "Auto" (the fan comes on as the stove heats and shuts off once it has cooled) or "Man" (bypasses the sensing device). Vacuum the grill openings on the back and bottom of the casing at least every six months (p. 10). Blowers, speed controls and thermal switches fall under the 3 year comprehensive warranty (p. 25).

Confirm the fan current: the blower section gives 115 volts A.C.-1.02 amps (p. 20); the rating label gives 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP (p. 3).

index_extra.p: Signs of a chimney fire and what to do
Inspect at least every two months in the heating season
The finish cures over the first 2-3 fires
Unsplit logs, charred on high before turning down
Unlock, pull ashes in, lock, empty the pan
4" Intake Starter and metal flex; required in mobile homes
Non-combustible floor protector sizes, USA and Canada

conflicts.issue: Maximum wood length: "Maximum Wood Length 20 inches" (ideal 16-18 inches) in the Efficiency and BTU Output table vs "length (up to 18"(457mm))" in Normal Operation.
Screws at the stove collar: single-wall pipe "secured at every joint and collar with 3 sheet metal screws" (p. 14) vs "Use holes provided in collar to secure pipe with two screws" (p. 15).

Connector through combustible walls: rating label says "DO NOT PASS A CHIMNEY CONNECTOR THROUGH A COMBUSTIBLE WALL OR CEILING"; p. 14 allows passage through a combustible wall conforming to CAN/CSA-B365, and pp. 18-19 show NFPA 211 pass-through Systems A-D.
Blower current: "115 volts A.C.-1.02 amps" (Optional Blower) vs "115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP" (rating label).

Rating label inch and mm values disagree for the Alderlea T6 sidewall-to-connector clearances: 24.6 in. / 612 mm (residential double-wall), 27.6 in. / 688 mm (alcove), 29.6 in. /739 mm (mobile home). The other T6 label values agree in both units.

review.notes: The p. 3 rating label is bilingual, shared with the Summit LE and Summit Classic LE, and its text is extracted out of order. Clearances in the guide are the label's Alderlea T6 values, matched by the label's own letter key (A sidewall to unit ... F corner to connector); the A/B/C values match the numbers in Figs. 5 and 12. The p. 3 Efficiency and BTU Output table is also out of order: HHV 74% / LHV 80% follows the manual's own definitions (HHV includes the energy to vaporize water) and matches the catalog; ideal 16-18 / maximum 20 inches follows max >= ideal. Not transcribed: Fig. 2 overall dimensions (p. 11, five unlabeled numbers) and the connector dimensions in Figs. 5 and 12 (e.g. 17 5/8", 20 1/8", 28 3/4"), which run about 3" more than the label's connector clearances and don't say what they measure to; only the clearly captioned Fig. 6/7 callouts (48" to combustibles in front, 7' minimum ceiling) are used. The label's floor-protector letters G/H/I (USA 16/5/0 in., Canada 18/8/8 in.) aren't defined in text; the guide uses p. 12 (USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the loading door opening), but the label's USA 5"/0" values may deserve a look. Alcove minimum width appears only in French on the label (LARGEUR 4 PIEDS/1.2M): not translated or used. p. 15 points to "Figure #3, Page 7" for floor outside air; Fig. 3 is the USA floor protector (p. 12) and the air inlet is shown in Fig. 6 (p. 16). p. 14 says both chimney system and connector must be listed yet also allows single-wall 24 gauge black pipe; both are quoted as printed. The baffle gasket is "#139.5" on p. 10 but part 80000365 in the parts list (p. 26); no gasket number is used. Warranty heading reads "LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)", shown as printed. The manual gives no weight, firebox volume, heating area, burn time, maximum cordwood BTU, view area or glass area, so those catalog specs are unchecked; catalog max log length 20 matches p. 3 but not p. 7 (18"). Catalog marks this model not for sale in the USA. No scrambled-font or French-only safety text needed decoding.
